note.explanation: A fire extinguisher and safety shower help people respond to emergencies in a laboratory. Students should know where they are and should be trained before using emergency equipment.
note.checkAnswer: Emergency drills should be compulsory so students practise responding calmly and safely.
note.simple: Know where the emergency equipment is. Practise what to do before an emergency happens.
note.checkQuestion: Why should students take part in emergency drills?
note.title: Fire Extinguishers and Emergency Drills
steps: Know where the portable fire extinguisher is kept.
Learn how to handle and apply it during a training session.
Know where the safety shower is and how it works.
Follow the laboratory's emergency instructions calmly.
note.answer: Students should know the location of the fire extinguisher and safety shower and learn how to use them. Emergency drills help them practise responding to an emergency without panic.

options: Only the teacher needs to know where it is
All students should know where it is placed
It should be kept outside the laboratory
Students should move it after each experiment
mcqs.stem: According to this section, who should know the location of the laboratory fire extinguisher?
rationales: This is incorrect because the section says students should be aware of its location.
This is correct because the section says all students should know where the extinguisher is placed.
This is incorrect because the section does not say to keep it outside the laboratory.
This is incorrect because the section does not tell students to move the extinguisher.

options: To train students to handle and apply the extinguisher
To teach students to hide chemicals
To practise carrying equipment out of the laboratory
To let students test the extinguisher during experiments
mcqs.stem: What is the purpose of a fire-extinguisher training session?
rationales: This is correct because training teaches students how to handle and apply the extinguisher properly.
This is incorrect because hiding chemicals is not the purpose of the training session.
This is incorrect because the section describes training to use the extinguisher, not to carry equipment out.
This is incorrect because the section does not recommend testing the extinguisher during experiments.

options: Only when an experiment is completed
Without any panic or harm to anybody
Only after leaving the building
Without telling anyone where it is
mcqs.stem: How should students learn to use the fire extinguisher?
rationales: This is incorrect because the section describes using it to control a small fire, not waiting until an experiment is completed.
This is correct because the section says students should learn to extinguish fire properly without panic or harm.
This is incorrect because the section does not say to use the extinguisher only after leaving the building.
This is incorrect because students should know the extinguisher's location.

options: A safety shower
A fume cupboard
A chemical store
A portable balance
mcqs.stem: Which other emergency facility does this section say should be available in the laboratory?
rationales: This is correct because the section says a shower facility should also be available.
This is incorrect because a fume cupboard is not the facility named in this section.
This is incorrect because the section does not identify a chemical store as the other emergency facility.
This is incorrect because a portable balance is not an emergency facility described here.

options: Everyone working in the laboratory should know its location and working
Only visitors should know where it is
It should be used only during training
Its location should be kept secret
mcqs.stem: What should laboratory workers know about the safety shower?
rationales: This is correct because the section says its location and working must be told to everybody working in the laboratory.
This is incorrect because the section refers to everybody working in the laboratory, not only visitors.
This is incorrect because the shower is an emergency facility, not an item for training use only.
This is incorrect because workers need to know where the shower is.

options: Emergency drills should be optional
Students should know how to face an emergency
Students should wait for a fire to practise
Only the laboratory in-charge needs emergency training
mcqs.stem: Which statement best follows the advice in this section?
rationales: This is incorrect because practising emergency responses is important for preparedness.
This is correct because the section says students should know how to face an emergency situation.
This is incorrect because students should receive training before an actual emergency.
This is incorrect because the section stresses that all students should be aware and trained.

written.text: How fire caused by chemicals should be handled?
written.finalAnswer: A small fire should be controlled with a portable fire extinguisher by a student trained to handle and apply it, without panic or harm to anybody.

rubric.why: The section identifies a portable fire extinguisher as the equipment used to control a small fire.

rubric.how: State that the extinguisher is used to control a small fire.

rubric.why: Students need to learn how to use the equipment properly and safely.

rubric.how: Mention training and safe, calm use.

modelAnswer: A portable fire extinguisher can quickly be used to control a small fire.

written.text: Why emergency drills are important to face emergency situations?
written.finalAnswer: Emergency drills are important because they train students to know how to face an emergency situation and respond without panic.

written.text: How will you handle an emergency situation caused by fire due to short circuiting?
written.finalAnswer: Raise the alarm and inform the teacher or laboratory in-charge immediately. Follow the laboratory emergency instructions; do not use water on electrical equipment. Use a fire extinguisher only if trained and it is safe to do so, and leave the laboratory if the fire cannot be controlled safely.

rubric.why: Promptly alerting the responsible person helps protect everyone.
rubric.description: Raises the alarm and informs the teacher or laboratory in-charge.

rubric.why: A short-circuit fire needs a safe response, not an unsafe attempt to put it out.
rubric.description: Follows laboratory emergency instructions and avoids using water on electrical equipment.
rubric.how: Mention following instructions and not using water on electrical equipment.

rubric.why: The section describes extinguisher use after students have been trained.
rubric.description: Uses an extinguisher only if trained and safe to do so.
rubric.how: Link use of the extinguisher to training and safety.

rubric.why: Leaving an unsafe area protects people if the fire cannot be controlled.
rubric.description: Leaves the laboratory if it is not safe to control the fire.
rubric.how: State that people should move to safety if the fire cannot be dealt with safely.

written.text: Put forward at least two suggestions to improve safety in the lab.
written.finalAnswer: Keep a portable fire extinguisher available and make sure all students know its location. Hold training sessions so students learn to use it, and make sure everyone knows the location and working of the safety shower.

rubric.description: Suggests providing a portable fire extinguisher.
rubric.how: Name the extinguisher as a laboratory safety measure.

rubric.why: Knowing the location allows students to find emergency equipment quickly.
rubric.description: Says all students should know where the extinguisher is.
rubric.how: Mention informing or teaching all students about its location.

rubric.why: Training helps students use the extinguisher properly.
rubric.description: Suggests training students to handle and apply the extinguisher.
rubric.how: Include a training session as a safety suggestion.

rubric.why: The section also recommends an available shower facility that workers know how to use.
rubric.description: Mentions providing a safety shower and telling people its location and working.
rubric.how: Name the shower and say workers should know its location or operation.

modelAnswer: Keep a portable fire extinguisher available in the laboratory and make sure all students know its location.

written.text: A student has spilled over a corrosive and explosive chemical due to an accident. Which emergency measures you will take to tackle the situation.
written.finalAnswer: Warn others and inform the teacher or laboratory in-charge immediately. Do not touch or try to clean up the chemical; keep people away and follow the laboratory emergency instructions. If there is fire, use a fire extinguisher only if trained and it is safe. Use the safety shower only as directed for an appropriate emergency, and leave the area if it is unsafe.

rubric.why: The responsible laboratory staff need to manage a hazardous spill.
rubric.description: Warns others and immediately informs the teacher or laboratory in-charge.
rubric.how: State that the responsible adult or laboratory in-charge must be told.

rubric.why: Keeping people away reduces the chance of injury or exposure.
rubric.description: Keeps people away from the spill and does not touch it.
rubric.how: Clearly say not to touch or approach the spilled chemical.

rubric.why: The correct response depends on the chemical and the laboratory's emergency procedure.
rubric.description: Follows the laboratory emergency instructions rather than attempting an untrained cleanup.
rubric.how: Say to follow the emergency procedure and leave cleanup to trained staff.

rubric.why: The section recommends extinguisher use for a small fire only by someone who has learned to use it.
rubric.description: For a fire, uses an extinguisher only if trained and it is safe.
rubric.how: Link any extinguisher use to training and safety.

rubric.why: Moving to safety or using the appropriate emergency facility helps protect people from harm.
rubric.description: States that people should leave if unsafe and identifies the shower as an emergency facility when appropriate.
rubric.how: Mention moving away from danger and using the shower only as directed.

modelAnswer: Warn others and inform the teacher or laboratory in-charge immediately.
Do not touch or try to clean up the chemical; keep people away and follow the laboratory emergency instructions.
If there is fire, use a fire extinguisher only if trained and it is safe.
Use the safety shower only as directed for an appropriate emergency.
Leave the area if it is unsafe.

examTips: A short-answer question may ask why emergency drills are important; say that they train students to face emergencies and respond without panic.
A constructed-response question may describe a laboratory fire; identify who to alert and explain that extinguisher use requires training.
For a question about emergency equipment, name both the portable fire extinguisher and the safety shower, and state that students should know their locations.
In a longer answer, organise the response in order: alert others, follow instructions, use equipment only when trained and safe, and move away from danger.
Marks are usually earned for naming the correct equipment, explaining its purpose, and giving safe actions in a clear sequence.

explain.title: Fire extinguisher
explain.body: Your textbook says: “Chemical laboratories using such materials which are likely to catch fire during experiments must have a portable fire extinguisher.” It can quickly be used to control a small fire. Students should know where it is and learn how to use it.

explain.title: Training and calm action
explain.body: Your textbook says: “A training session should be held to train all the students to know how to handle and apply this fire extinguisher to extinguish the fire properly without any panic or harm to anybody.” Training helps students act properly instead of panicking.

explain.title: Safety shower and emergency awareness
explain.body: Your textbook says: “Similarly the facility of a shower should also be made available in the lab whose location and working must be told to everybody working in the lab.” Everyone should know where the shower is and how it works, and should know how to face an emergency.

mistakes: Do not say that only the teacher needs to know where the extinguisher is; the section says all students should know its location.
Do not confuse knowing where equipment is with knowing how to use it; training is needed for proper extinguisher use.
Do not suggest using emergency equipment without training or without regard to safety.
Do not omit the safety shower when asked about the emergency facilities described in this section.
Do not answer a question about drills with only “they are important”; explain that they train students to face emergencies.
